content:
Mathematician Terence Tao and OpenAI’s Mark Chen discuss how AI is transforming scientific research and mathematics, shifting the field from solitary work to a collaborative, dynamic marketplace of ideas. AI now handles routine tasks, enabling researchers to act as orchestrators of discovery while amateurs and students contribute meaningfully using new tools.

• AI automates tedious tasks like coding and literature reviews, freeing top researchers to direct multiple projects as high-level orchestrators  
• Due to AI's jagged capabilities—strong in some areas, weak in others—human collaboration remains crucial, especially in verifying and guiding results  
• Challenge sets like the Erdos problems allow amateurs and students with AI assistance to solve overlooked puzzles, democratizing mathematical discovery  
• Education is shifting from rote homework to project-based learning, emphasizing prompt design and formal verification, though overreliance on AI risks cognitive offloading and lost learning depth
source: Fields Medal recipient Terence Tao, and OpenAI’s CRO Mark Chen @UCLA
